name: Sasha Kovalenko
headline: 54, lawyer on medical leave, trust fund manager, Lviv
title: A Walk Before the Ledger
situation: It is 8:10 a.m., and Sasha is on the living room floor midway through their stretching routine, right leg lifted onto a folded towel. The doorbell rings—it's Marta from upstairs, who knows about the recovery. She's heading to the farmers' market and says she can wait ten minutes if Sasha wants to join her for a slow walk in the sun. The air would be good, and she's ready to leave now. But Sasha still needs to finish the remaining repetitions and write today's ledger entry before the Tuesday files arrive at nine. Marta is waiting for an answer.

context.relationship_profiles: Marta is the neighbor who brought Sasha a pot of borscht the first week after the accident, and she has since checked in every few days, always careful not to push. Sasha appreciates her kindness but also knows she tends to linger with small talk after any invitation. They have joined her for brief walks twice before, both times cutting the outing short to get back to the ledgers.
context.tendencies: When a physical therapy session is incomplete, Sasha has repeatedly postponed errands, phone calls, and even meals to finish the sequence and write the ledger entry. During earlier recovery weeks, Sasha declined three similar walk invitations from neighbors and colleagues, citing the Tuesday file drop or the therapist's schedule. On the rare occasions Sasha accepted an interruption, they returned visibly tense and rewrote the day's assessment entry with extra care.
context.current_state: Sasha's right quadriceps is mildly aching from the repetitions done so far, and the bruise along the ribs still twinges when they twist. The morning coffee is half-finished and cold on the side table. Sasha has been awake since 6:45, and the anticipation of the Tuesday files has already tightened their jaw slightly.
context.immediate_memories: The doorbell sound reminds Sasha of the morning Marta first came down with the borscht, when Sasha had to pause mid-stretch and ended up forgetting the exact number of repetitions for that day's set. The sun through the living room window cues a memory of the physiotherapist's warning that fresh air helps bone healing, but also that consistency matters more than occasional excursions.
context.reflective_memories: Sasha recalls from their teaching years that a single missed session could throw off a semester's syllabus, and they applied the same principle to legal deadlines. They also remember that their grandfather used to take a short walk every morning regardless of weather, and called it 'clearing the head for the work ahead,' though he never skipped his own morning reading. Sasha has noticed that on days they have accepted social breaks, the ledger's 'subjective assessment' column tends to read 'distracted' rather than 'improved.'
